findings.title: KeyError when Integration metadata has no `sender`
findings.body: `integration.metadata["sender"]["login"]` assumes every existing GitHub Integration row has a `sender` entry. `build_integration` only sets `sender` when it is present in state. Integrations created by older code or by other paths will lack it. For those, reaching this branch (an Integration exists without an OrganizationIntegration) raises KeyError and returns a 500 instead of the intended error page. Use `.get()` and fail closed with `error(...)`.

findings.title: User/installation match is skipped when the Integration row doesn't exist yet
findings.body: The new sender-vs-authenticated-user check runs only on the path where an Integration already exists (created by the installation webhook). If no Integration exists, `pipeline.next_step()` is called with no validation. That happens when the webhook is delayed, failed, or hasn't been processed yet. In that case a user can still finish the pipeline with an arbitrary `installation_id` they did not install and bind it to their own Sentry org. The check should also run here, e.g. by comparing against the installation's account or sender fetched from the GitHub API.

findings.title: Network/API failures in the OAuth exchange produce 500s
findings.body: `safe_urlopen(...)` is called outside the try block, and `get_user_info(...)` is not wrapped either. A connection error, timeout, or a non-JSON or error response from GitHub raises an unhandled exception. The user then gets a 500 rather than the 'Invalid installation request' page described in the PR.

findings.title: OAuth authorize URL parameters are not URL-encoded
findings.body: The authorize URL is built with an f-string, so `redirect_uri` (which contains `:` and `/`) and the other parameters are not percent-encoded. A redirect URI containing `?` or `&` would corrupt the query string. Use `urlencode` for the parameters.

findings.title: Non-active existing Integrations now always fail installation
findings.body: Before this change, an existing Integration with no OrganizationIntegration proceeded to the next step regardless of status. Now, if the Integration is not ACTIVE (e.g. disabled), the lookup with `status=ObjectStatus.ACTIVE` raises DoesNotExist. The user then sees a generic 'Invalid installation request' error, which blocks reinstalling such integrations and gives a misleading message.

findings.title: test_installation_not_found no longer tests the 404 path
findings.body: The test now sends a deliberately wrong `state` (`ddd023...`), so it fails at the state-signature check. It asserts the generic 'Invalid installation request.' message. The original assertion for 'The GitHub installation could not be found.' was removed, so nothing covers the 404 branch in `build_integration` any more. The test name is now misleading. Add separate tests for the state-mismatch case and the installation-404 case.
